items.title: The J-0 property descends along an injective finite type map of domains
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the J-0 property, meaning that the regular locus is open, descends from a finite type extension of domains to the base, and the proof is an 8-line argument of two reductions. It first localises the target at a nonzero element so that the extension becomes regular, then applies generic flatness to make the extension faithfully flat over a further localisation, at which point the descent of regularity along a faithfully flat map gives the conclusion. Both reductions are performed by named statements of the Algebra chapter, and the localisations are chosen so that the hypotheses of those statements are met, which is where the brevity of the proof hides its content.
